universities.summary: NIFT Chennai is the Chennai campus of the statutory National Institute of Fashion Technology, established in 1995. Its core degree portfolio combines six design specialisations, apparel production and postgraduate fashion management. Design studios, technical laboratories and industry-linked projects support these different study routes.
universities.campusLifestyle: Studios, laboratories, workshops and a resource centre support creative practice alongside classroom learning. The Chennai campus also has an auditorium, fitness centre, sports facilities and a courtyard amphitheatre. Hostel availability and allocation should be checked separately from an academic offer.
universities.cityProfile: The campus is on Rajiv Gandhi Salai in Taramani, Chennai, Tamil Nadu. This profile covers the Chennai campus rather than the NIFT network as a whole. Applicants choosing a campus during seat allocation should use the Chennai address when planning accommodation, travel and the practicalities of attending studio and laboratory sessions.
universities.practicalExposure: The design degrees combine material exploration, studio projects and interdisciplinary learning. Apparel Production adds specialised laboratories, live industry projects, internships and a graduation project across garment engineering and manufacturing. Fashion Management focuses on the commercial side of the industry. The shared NIFT curriculum also includes industry visits and real-world projects; none of these activities guarantees a placement.
universities.hostelOverview: Chennai has hostel facilities, and campus induction includes hostel affairs. An academic allocation is not itself confirmation of a hostel room; check room availability, allotment conditions and current charges with the campus.
universities.dietarySupport: Meal plans, special diets and allergy arrangements need to be discussed with the campus before accepting accommodation; the reviewed Chennai pages do not establish a guaranteed dietary service.
universities.safetyOverview: The Chennai site provides an Internal Complaint Committee section with committee information and harassment-redressal material. Applicants can use that channel to identify the relevant reporting procedure; it is not a guarantee that incidents cannot occur.
universities.studentSupport: Campus induction introduces academic guidance, student services, the Campus Management System and hostel affairs. The campus also provides access to its resource centre and student-affairs information.
whyChoose: Choose among six distinct design specialisations without confusing them with the apparel-technology degree.
Apparel Production combines manufacturing laboratories with industry-linked projects and internships.
The separate international admissions route accepts SAT for undergraduate degrees and GMAT for Fashion Management.
thingsToConsider: Regular and international/NRI applicants have different selection procedures and substantially different fee schedules.
The 2026 dates are a completed admissions cycle, not confirmation of a future application window.
Short diploma and continuing-education courses depend on minimum enrolment and are not substitutes for the four-year degrees.
bestFitFor: Applicants seeking studio-led design study in a clearly identified fashion or product specialisation.
Applicants with the required mathematics background who prefer apparel manufacturing and technology.
Graduates seeking fashion-business study and able to meet the correct regular or international selection route.

faq.question: Which degrees are available at NIFT Chennai?
faq.answer: The campus lists B.Des in Accessory Design, Fashion Communication, Fashion Design, Knitwear Design, Leather Design and Textile Design; B.F.Tech in Apparel Production; and Master of Fashion Management.

faq.question: How long are the main degree programmes?
faq.answer: The B.Des and B.F.Tech routes take four years. Master of Fashion Management takes two years. Short diploma and continuing-education courses have separate durations and entry rules.

faq.question: Can international applicants apply?
faq.answer: Foreign nationals, NRI, OCI, PIO and SAARC applicants have a separate admissions category. It requires category evidence, suitable academic qualifications and working knowledge of English. Foreign qualifications need the prescribed equivalence.

faq.question: Which entrance tests apply to overseas-category applicants?
faq.answer: The international category uses SAT for B.Des and B.F.Tech, and GMAT for Master of Fashion Management. These applicants do not use the regular NIFT entrance examination; campus and programme allocation follows score-based merit and preferences.

faq.question: Is mathematics needed for every undergraduate degree?
faq.answer: Mathematics is required for the 10+2 route into B.F.Tech. The B.Des 10+2 route does not impose that subject condition. Accepted diploma and equivalent-qualification routes have their own requirements.

faq.question: What does the quoted annual fee cover?
faq.answer: INR 907,000 is the 2026–27 NRI-category annual tuition at Chennai for two semesters. It excludes other academic charges and living costs. Regular-category tuition is separately published at INR 150,000 per semester.

faq.question: Is teaching in English?
faq.answer: NIFT explicitly identifies English as its teaching medium. Applicants in the international category must also possess working knowledge of English.

faq.question: Does admission guarantee accommodation or employment?
faq.answer: No such guarantee is established here. Chennai has hostel facilities, but rooms require separate confirmation. Internships, projects and career preparation are academic opportunities rather than guaranteed employment.

faq.question: Are the 2026 application dates still usable?
faq.answer: No. The deadlines in the cited 2026 cycle have passed. Applicants should use the relevant new admissions notice rather than assume the same dates will recur.

admissionsContent.overview: A four-year design degree specialising in accessory design, with studio, material and project-based learning. Regular and international applicants have different selection routes.

eligibility.intro: Admission depends on the qualification and applicant-category requirements for this programme.
items: Pass recognised 10+2, NIOS with at least five subjects, or an accepted equivalent qualification.
Alternatively, a three- or four-year diploma recognised by AICTE or a State Board after Class 10 can qualify.
Regular undergraduate applicants must be under 24 on 1 August of the admission year; SC, ST and PwD applicants receive a five-year relaxation.
Applicants using a foreign qualification must obtain the required equivalence; international-category applicants need working knowledge of English.

applicationSteps: Choose the correct applicant category and check its qualification and age conditions before registering online.
Regular-route applicants complete GAT, CAT and a Situation Test and participate in the applicable merit-based seat-allocation process.
International-category applicants apply through NIFT admissions and arrange official SAT (institution code 7258) score delivery; campus and programme allocation depends on merit and preferences.
Submit original qualification/category documents for verification and pay the applicable fees after allocation.
